transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Um, I guess I came in because... well, ever since my sister and her baby moved back home, I’ve just been a lot more on edge and down than usual. I find myself snapping over really little stuff around the house. And then, by the time I show up to class or to the shop for work, I'm already completely drained. 

I mean, I’m still getting by, but I’ve missed a couple of deadlines lately. I even had to back out of helping build the theater set at school because I just couldn’t keep everything straight anymore. It's just been a lot to handle.
Before your sister and her baby moved in, did you feel like you were generally functioning well and feeling like yourself, or had you been struggling with these moods for a long time?

No, I was doing okay before they moved in. I felt pretty much like myself. The trouble really just started... maybe within a couple of weeks of them getting there. Once the house got really crowded, that's when I started feeling this way and getting so drained. Before that, I was managing school and work just fine.
Aside from feeling on edge, have you been feeling persistently sad, hopeless, or like you have lost interest in the things you used to enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or hopeless, really. Just... tired, I guess. And I haven't lost interest in stuff I like. I still want to do things, like the theater set, I just... I don't have the energy for it right now with everything going on at the house. But it's not like I don't care anymore.
When you describe feeling 'down,' is it more that you are feeling worried or anxious about the situation at home, or do you feel a sense of sadness or emptiness?

Um, I wouldn't really say it's either of those. I don't feel empty, and I'm not really worried or anxious about anything bad happening at home. It's more just... I guess I'm just stressed out because the house is so crowded and loud now. It's just a lot of chaos to deal with day in and day out. So when I say down, I just mean I'm frustrated and worn out by it all, not really sad or worried.
Even though you don't feel sad or empty, have you noticed any changes in your appetite, sleep, or ability to concentrate since this started?

No, not really. I mean, I'm still eating the same as always. My sleep is fine, too. I guess... well, I can concentrate just fine when I'm at work or in class. It's just when I'm at home that I can't really focus on anything, but that's mostly because it's so loud with the baby and everyone around, you know? But yeah, my appetite and sleep and all that hasn't really changed.

Do you feel that your level of frustration and the difficulty you are having with your daily responsibilities is significantly greater than what most people would experience when dealing with a crowded home?

Not really, no. I mean... I think anyone would be pretty frustrated living with a crying baby and just having no space to themselves. It's a lot to handle all at once. So, I don't think my reaction is way worse than what most people would feel in this situation. It's just really annoying to deal with, that's all.
